stem: A support tie would constrict or abrade a stem if installed exactly where first planned. What should Technician I do?
choices: Install the tie tightly at the planned point because following the original position is more important than minor rubbing.
Cut or notch the stem slightly so the tie can fit without shifting the planned position.
Skip the support task entirely and leave no record of the conflict.
Use the permitted adjustment or escalate the conflict rather than knowingly installing the support in a way that constricts or abrades tissue.
rationale: The purpose of a support is to protect or guide the plant, not injure it. If the planned position would constrict or abrade the stem, Technician I should use an authorized adjustment or escalate rather than knowingly causing tissue damage. The work standard should be met safely, with exceptions documented when needed.
